literal: Greatly sweet is fools' friendship; at separation, pain-giving thing, there is not one.
translation: The friendship of fools is highly pleasant, for when it ends, it leaves behind no pain at all.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களுடன் கொள்ளும் நட்பு மிகவும் இனிமையானது; ஏனெனில், அவர்களைப் பிரியும்போது நமக்கு எந்தத் துன்பமும் ஏற்படுவதில்லை.
explanation: This couplet uses deep irony to describe the nature of associating with foolish people. It states that the friendship of fools is exceedingly sweet. The reason for this sweetness is revealed in the second line: when the friendship ends, it causes absolutely no pain or sorrow. Unlike true friendship, which brings immense grief upon separation, parting from a fool brings only relief. The word 'கேண்மை' denotes friendship, while 'பீழை' means distress, highlighting the contrast between the expected sorrow of parting and the actual relief felt when a fool leaves.
